newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas call for mobilization against vote.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas call for mobilization against vote.

text.p: Nicaragua's left-wing Sandinista Front late on Monday called for a national mobilisation to fight alleged irregularities and fraud in the October 20 general elections.

At an extraordinary meeting of the Sandinista Assembly, the party's highest body presided by former President Daniel Ortega, members listed a litany of election irregularities they said made it "impossible to know with certainty the electorate's decision."

In a spoken statement, Sandinista leaders called on the people "defend the vote through distinct forms of civic protest such as the collection of signatures, assemblies and other forms of popular mobilisation."
The Sandinista leadership also called for elections to be annuled and new elections held in the populous provinces of Managua and Matagalpa, which together have more than half Nicaragua's population.
Outside the Sandinista Assembly more than 100 party activists chanted "Fraud! Fraud!" to the television cameras and vowed not to let their right-wing rivals rob them of their victory.

More than two weeks after the vote, apparently won by Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance, Nicaragua's Supreme Election Council (CSE) still has not announced official winners, leaving the country in political suspense.
Aleman, the former mayor of Managua, leads Ortega, who headed Nicaragua's 1979-1990 left-wing Sandinista government, 49 to 38 percent in the preliminary vote count.

While Aleman has already claimed victory, accepting the congratulations of world leaders and naming his cabinet, Ortega has refused to concede defeat, saying he will wait till the CSE has finished reviewing the vote count.
The threat of a post-election clash between Nicaragua's two major political forces has caused tensions to soar and the police to ban all public demonstrations for fear of violence.

"Given the magnitude of the countless irregularities and shamelessly fraudulent actions found, the Sandinista Assembly considers that the great loser of the October 20 elections were democracy and the Nicaraguan people," the party statement said.

Among the alleged irregularities are missing or adulterated vote-tally sheets, numerical discrepancies in the count, illegal personnel working in the voting booths and inaccurate telegrams of voting results sent to CSE headquarters.

The Sandinistas said it was "particularly worrying that the provinces with the highest number of anomalies were Managua, Matagalpa and Jinotega, provinces were the president of the regional election councils were from the Liberal Alliance."

After skirting around the issue for weeks, Sandinista leadership has come as directly as they ever have of accusing their right-wing rivals of election fraud and calling for their grass roots activists to start protesting to vote's results.
The CSE has said it will announce the official winners in mid-November after it finishes reviewing the disputed vote count.
